A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BOA research by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial experimental and structural revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments, including perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, processing times and calibration-seed sensitivity results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original weight-only and weight–activation quantization experiments, comparator evaluations and a runtime ablation in Sections 3–4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: BOA's attention-aware Hessians, relaxation, Kronecker-based computations and head-wise quantization/update procedure are retained. The new experiments combine this unchanged weight algorithm with existing QuaRot/SpinQuant transformations and conventional activation/KV quantizers. Simplified GPTQ pseudocode omits batching details without introducing a different quantization rule.

E1.justification: v2 retains WikiText-2, ARC-challenge, ARC-easy and HellaSwag, removes C4, PTB and MMLU evaluations, and adds BoolQ, LAMBADA, OpenBookQA, PIQA and WinoGrande. This substantially changes the represented language-modeling and zero-shot task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated SmoothQuant and Z-FOLD combinations disappear. v2 adds QuaRot-RTN/GPTQ, SpinQuant-RTN/GPTQ and DuQuant with and without learnable weight clipping, while retaining OmniQuant and AffineQuant. RTN also gains zero-shot comparison rows. GPTQ is the renamed OPTQ baseline, not a newly added method.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes calibration from C4 to WikiText-2 while retaining 128 sequences of 2048 tokens. The model suite drops BLOOM and adds LLaMA-7B, LLaMA2, LLaMA3 and LLaMA3.2 configurations. New evaluations introduce transformed-model controls and activation/KV precision combinations such as W2A4KV4; reported zero-shot averages now cover eight tasks instead of four.

E4.justification: v1's calibration-sampling sensitivity analysis in Appendix C.4 disappears. v2 adds a targeted ablation of head-wise simultaneous quantization: Table 2 reports 135.4 versus 3.295 hours on LLaMA-30B without versus with it. The new comparisons also evaluate DuQuant with and without weight clipping.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C.4 reports five calibration seeds—0, 10, 20, 50 and 100—plus means and standard deviations for INT2/INT3 OPT results. v2 removes this entire uncertainty-reporting component and supplies no corresponding seed, repeated-run or dispersion information. This establishes a reporting removal, not that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced, added and removed. For example, OPT-125M INT2 WikiText-2 perplexities for GPTQ/BOA change from 232.8/141.6 in v1 Table 2 to 411.3/85.63 in v2 Table 9. Calibration differs, so these are replaced results rather than a matched-setting improvement. v2 additionally reports newer-model, transformation, activation/KV and runtime-ablation outcomes.

T1.justification: The substantive Hessian derivations, independence assumptions, Kronecker/Cholesky reasoning and Appendix A–B proofs are retained. v2 Proposition 3.1 restates the row-update formula already derived in v1 Appendix B, Equation 19. Its promotion to a proposition does not add a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims improved backpropagation-free weight quantization, especially at low precision. v2's abstract and introduction additionally claim state-of-the-art weight–activation quantization through combination with outlier-suppression methods, and explicitly assert priority as the first backpropagation-free integer-weight optimizer considering inter-layer dependencies.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's limitations discussion about omitted fully connected-layer dependencies and the cost of full Transformer-block reconstruction. The activation-quantization limitation is superseded by experiments. v2 adds hardware-based justification for excluding mixed-precision methods, interprets the runtime ablation through GPU parallelism, and introduces an impact statement claiming real-time mobile/edge applicability.

D1.justification: v2 adds LET/LWC and use-ln-matrix settings, SpinQuant rotation-calibration choices, and per-token activation/KV quantization details; hardware changes from an 80-GB A100 to an 80-GB H100. It removes v1's disclosure of quantization-order selection and matched per-channel scale/zero-point optimization for BOA and OPTQ, and simplifies Appendix D by omitting blocksize-128 implementation details. These are documentation changes, not proof that every omitted setting changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially reframes BOA as integer-weight optimization complementary to smoothing, rotation and permutation methods. It adds discussion and citations for QuaRot, SpinQuant, DuQuant, SpQR and OAC, including reasons for excluding mixed-precision approaches. Earlier references including QuIP and OWQ disappear, and the introduction adds an explicit first-method positioning claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. The OPTQ review becomes a BOA overview within Method, experimental sections and Appendix C are reorganized, and Limitations is replaced by an Impact Statement. OPTQ terminology changes to GPTQ throughout, while the existing row-update result receives a prominent proposition statement.

P2.justification: Experimental tables are extensively redesigned: separate perplexity/accuracy displays and model-size columns become combined perplexity-plus-eight-task tables grouped by model and precision. New runtime tables appear, and Table 1 explicitly contrasts GPTQ with BOA. Figures 1–2 retain their essential content but are resized/repositioned; running headers and denser table layouts change the document's presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful weight–activation evidence addressing an explicit v1 limitation, broader contemporary comparisons and a direct efficiency ablation. However, it removes the five-seed uncertainty study, important comparator-setting disclosures and the unresolved full-block limitation. Table 6 also repeats complete DuQuant and DuQuant + LWC result rows across LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA2-13B without explanation. These gains coexist with reduced transparency and uncertainty about parts of the new evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
